summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on unit economics for Helix Medical's clinical summarization and triage workload. Discussed workload sizing, per-token cost levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and a plan to run a 48 hour benchmark on Dedicated. Agreed to exchange cost model spreadsheet and traffic traces; Redwood to provision test capacity and run benchmarks; follow-up to review results and finalize pilot terms.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz, Samir Khan, Priya Desai, Aaron Holt

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, I think the goal for today is scoping the POC for cost modeling and unit economics, right? confirm that that's still the goal.
[00:06] Dr. Elena Ruiz: yes exactly, we want to understand cost per active user for our clinical summarize/triage flow, and see how Redwood's batching/caching impacts our unit economics.
[00:15] Samir: hi, quick intro \b i'm Samir, CTO, high level constraints \b latency needs to stay under ~300ms p95 for triage, budget target is roughly $X per active user per month but we'll translate to per-token.
[00:27] Maya: great, i'll hand to Jordan for the workload sizing questions, and then we'll talk benchmarks.
[00:31] Jordan: cool, thanks. so Elena, what does an average request look like \b tokens in, tokens out, typical concurrency?
[00:36] Dr. Elena Ruiz: average input is about 220 tokens, output about 120 tokens, but we have long tails \b around 10% are > 1024. Concurrent active sessions are around 40-60 during peak, and bursts to 120 for a few minutes.
[00:49] Jordan: got it. do you have any caching opportunities \b for prefix caching or common templates?
[00:53] Priya Desai: yes, about 30% of requests reuse a template plus patient-specific fields; we think prefix/KV cache could help.
[00:58] Jordan: perfect, so rough arithmetic \b if we assume model A (open Llama-variant) at ~0.0004 $/token baseline hosted, we can push that down with batching and Dedicated pricing and quantized model variants.
[01:10] Dr. Elena Ruiz: can you give an example? like per-patient cost for our median flow?
[01:14] Jordan: sure, rough walk-through \b median request 340 total tokens, at baseline hosted price 0.0004 per token => $0.136 per request. With batching (effective 1.6x tokens/sec efficiency) and prefix cache covering 30% of tokens, plus int8 quantization on Dedicated we estimate unit cost could drop to ~ $0.03 - $0.05 per request. those are ballpark numbers \b we'll formalize in the spreadsheet.
[01:36] Samir: that's a big swing \b curious about latency impact though, quantization and batching could add to p95.
[01:41] Jordan: yes exactly. batching trades off latency for throughput; our Recommendation: for triage path keep a low-latency lane \b smaller batch size and prefer Dedicated reserved capacity to hit p95 targets. For background summarization you can use larger batches/night processing.
[01:55] Maya: also to note, Redwood has automatic workload-aware batching \b you can set latency SLOs per route so hot paths get prioritized.
[02:03] Dr. Elena Ruiz: ok interesting. benchmarks \b what would you run?
[02:07] Jordan: plan is a 48 hour benchmark on a Dedicated test pool that mirrors your expected concurrency. We'll replay your traces (Priya to share) with sampled distributions (seq length, prefix reuse). Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and failure/error rate.
[02:21] Priya Desai: we can export traces, is there a format preference?
[02:24] Jordan: JSON lines with timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens is easiest. we'll provide a small template.
[02:29] Aaron Holt: timeline \b how soon can we run this?
[02:32] Maya: we can start provisioning this week, provisioned Dedicated test environment in ~3 business days, then run 48 hours \b so earliest results back in ~10 days.
[02:43] Samir: ok makes sense.
[02:45] Jordan: a couple more knobs \b model variants (full fp16 vs int8), also sequence-length dependent kernel selection can change perf. we usually test two variants: quantized int8 for cost-optimized, and fp16 for latency-sensitive paths.
[02:58] Dr. Elena Ruiz: any guidance on how to set batching knobs?
[03:00] Jordan: we recommend starting with conservative batch sizes for triage (batch size 2-4, per-device concurrency tuned) and enable dynamic batching for background; we'll include recommended values in the spreadsheet and the benchmark will tune them automatically.
[03:13] Priya Desai: security/compliance \b we'll need SOC2, SSO/SAML details, and KMS/HSM usage for keys.
[03:20] Maya: yep we'll share our SOC2 report and the security pack; for keys Redwood can integrate with your KMS or customer-managed HSM in Private deployments.
[03:29] Samir: private deployment \b what are the cost implications?
[03:31] Jordan: Private or on-prem has higher fixed costs but gives you full network isolation; Dedicated reserved pools are middle ground \b cheaper per-token than hosted and still managed. We'll model both in the spreadsheet.
[03:42] Dr. Elena Ruiz: on success criteria \b besides latency and cost, we want quality parity within 2% of current production BLEU/ROUGE-ish metric and no regression on critical prompts.
[03:52] Jordan: we'll include a small eval harness to check a sample set of prompts and quality metrics pre/post.
[03:57] Maya: ok let's capture next steps \b i'll send the cost-model with scenarios: hosted fp16, dedicated fp16, dedicated int8, private baseline. Jordan will run benchmarks; Priya will send traces; Elena will provide the sample prompt set for quality checks.
[04:13] Aaron Holt: about budget constraints \b we have a soft cap for the pilot of $15k for the month, can you show examples of pilot configurations that fit under that?
[04:20] Maya: yes we'll run scenarios in the spreadsheet: expected tokens/month * per-token cost = monthly spend. we can also present 99th percentile cost with and without caching.
[04:29] Dr. Elena Ruiz: what about cold starts and KV cache warming?
[04:32] Jordan: cache warm-up will show a short initial spike; we can pre-warm common prefixes as part of the test. for cold-starts model load times depend on whether model is resident on the GPU pool; Dedicated keeps warm workers for reserved capacity.
[04:46] Samir: great. any blockers we foresee?
[04:48] Priya: nothing major; just need the template for traces and the NDA redacted security docs.
[04:52] Maya: we'll share security docs (link in follow up) and a simple traces template.
[04:58] Jordan: one more note \b batching efficiency numbers are workload dependent; our rule of thumb is 1.3-1.8x token efficiency improvement with batching on standard conversational workloads, but with prefix caching you can get additional effective savings. we'll encode these assumptions in the model.
[05:13] Dr. Elena Ruiz: good to know. how do you handle fallback if Dedicated capacity is exhausted?
[05:17] Jordan: we have smart routing and fallback policies \b requests can be routed to hosted fallbacks or other regions; you can set hard budget caps or prioritize critical routes. in the POC we'll test the fallback path as well.
[05:27] Samir: okay cool.
[05:29] Maya: any final Qs?
[05:31] Aaron Holt: just one \b can we see a worked example for a cohort of 10k active users?
[05:35] Maya: yes we'll include worked examples in the spreadsheet \b tokens per user assumptions, cache hit rates, batching gains, final monthly cost.
[05:42] Jordan: to summarize benchmarks and acceptance: run 48hr Dedicated replay of traces => target p95 < 300ms for triage (95% of requests), cost per request under $0.06 for triage median, quality regression < 2% on eval set. if we hit those we consider POC successful and move to pilot contract.
[05:59] Dr. Elena Ruiz: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:02] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the cost-model spreadsheet.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions; speaker labels approximate.
